MedicalJobsAustralia.com     Job Description:

Better and fairer care. Always.

We are St Vincent's Health Australia, Australia's largest not-for-profit provider of health and aged care services. 

Founded by The Sisters of Charity in 1857, our +30,000 healthcare superheroes operate public and private hospitals, residential aged care, community and virtual care, and outreach programs. 

About the role

Be part of a busy and collaborative team providing first and second-level technical support for computer systems, software, and hardware issues, both remotely and face-to-face.

Troubleshoot, monitor, and restore personal computers and devices connected to the network

Deliver high-quality client service, managing issues with integrity, compassion, and timely resolution

Work from various sites across our Hospital and Aged Care network to resolve technical incidents

Maintains telecommunications systems by installing, operating, and maintaining voice and data communications services.

Participate in the after-hours on-call roster

About you

Current Australian driver's license and reliable vehicle able to transport I.T. hardware and available after hours is MUST (cannot be a motorbike or scooter)

Certificate IV in Information Technology Support (or equivalent IT qualification)

Minimum 3+ years' experience in field engineering, desktop support or IT technical roles

Strong knowledge and skills in PC hardware and associated devices

Good understanding and associated skills in networking.

Must be able to commit to fulltime hours, including after-hours on-call requirements as detailed above

Why work at St Vincent's?

Join us on our mission to provide care to all, including the most at-risk people in our community

Discounted access to many gyms for you and your family with Fitness Passport

Access to discounted private health insurance with Medibank

Access to a salary sacrifice program (smart salary). Make a proportion of your salary tax-free!

Committed to financial support for educational development, scholarship programs, paid study leave

Sponsorship - work rights for Australia

Please note, visa sponsorship is not available for this position. For this role you must be an Australian or New Zealand citizen or have an Australia visa that grants you the work rights necessary for the role.

Pre-employment checks

Your employment is conditional upon the completion of all role-required pre-employment checks, including relevant immunisations.

Equal opportunity

We celebrate diversity & inclusion and are committed to equal employment opportunity for everyone.

How to apply

Please submit your resume and a brief cover letter highlighting how your interest, skills, and experience align with the role.

Respectfully, this role is not open to recruitment agencies.

About CALHN
At Central Adelaide (CALHN), we're shaping the future of health through excellence in clinical care, research, and innovation. As South Australia's largest health network, we deliver exceptional, safe and connected healthcare - for our patients, our community, and our people.

With more than 17,000 dedicated employees, every day at CALHN presents an opportunity to make a real impact-not because it's expected, but because our values guide us to be our best. Find out more about CALHN sites and services, our stories and the opportunities to be part of CALHN.

About the Role

As an Administration Assistant in the Parking Office, you'll keep services running smoothly by managing car parking, fleet, lost property and transport support. You'll coordinate requests, maintain records and provide friendly, efficient admin support across a busy healthcare environment.

Key responsibilities

- Manage car parking and permit requests
- Process expiation notices and follow up actions
- Maintain fleet vehicle records and bookings
- Support lost property and insurance claims
- Coordinate transport and admin enquiries
- Update systems and maintain accurate records
- Provide customer focused service to staff and public
- Liaise with internal teams and external stakeholders

About You

You're a highly organised Administration Assistant who takes pride in accuracy, service and keeping things running smoothly. You work well independently, communicate clearly and bring strong attention to detail in a busy environment.

- Proven admin experience with varied office duties
- Confident with MS Office and admin systems
- Strong data entry accuracy and attention to detail
- Prioritise workload and meet tight timeframes
- Communicate clearly with staff and public

Why You'll Love It Here - CALHN benefits that matter
We know that a great career is about more than just the work you do, it's also about the support you receive. At CALHN, you'll enjoy :

Salary packaging - up to $9,010 for living expenses + $2,650 for meals & entertainment + pre-tax super & novated lease options

Safe connections - be part of a culture of safety and connectivity, focusing on outcomes and continuous improvements

Recognition & growth - celebrate success and explore opportunities across CALHN's many sites

Flexible work options - speak to us about flexibility options for this role to suit your lifestyle

Paid leave - with leave loading for rest and recharge

Health & fitness perks - discounted access to Fitness Passport & free flu vaccinations

Wellbeing support - Employee Assistance Program for you & your family

Diversity & Inclusion
We're committed to building an inclusive workplace where everyone feels safe, respected, and supported. We strongly encourage applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, people with disabilities, culturally diverse backgrounds, and LGBTQIA+ communities.

Safety Advisor / Occupational Health and Safety Advisor – Full-Time
Location: Welshpool, Western Australia 6106
Employment Type: Full-Time
Salary: $100,000 – $130,000 per annum (depending on skills and experience)

MINPROVISE INTERNATIONAL PTY LTD is a leading total solutions provider delivering specialist maintenance and shutdown services, engineering, fabrication, project services, and sustaining capital works. We also provide a comprehensive range of equipment and products, supporting the mining, oil & gas, and construction industries across Australia and internationally.

We are currently seeking an experienced and motivated Safety Advisor / Occupational Health and Safety Advisor to join our growing team on a full-time basis.

About the Role
As a Safety Advisor / Occupational Health and Safety Advisor, you will be responsible for supporting the implementation, monitoring, and continuous improvement of workplace health and safety systems across mining, engineering, maintenance, fabrication, and industrial projects. You will work closely with project managers, supervisors, employees, and contractors to ensure compliance with legislation, company policies, and client safety requirements.

Key Responsibilities
•	Implement, maintain, and monitor workplace health and safety systems, policies, and procedures.
•	Provide advice and guidance to management, supervisors, and employees on occupational health and safety matters.
•	Conduct workplace inspections, audits, risk assessments, and safety observations.
•	Identify workplace hazards and recommend appropriate control measures to minimise risks.
•	Assist with incident investigations, reporting, root cause analysis, and corrective actions.
•	Develop, review, and maintain safety documentation, including SWMS, JSA, risk assessments, and safety reports.
•	Monitor compliance with WHS legislation, Australian Standards, client requirements, and company procedures.
•	Deliver safety inductions, toolbox talks, and training sessions to employees and contractors.
•	Promote a strong safety culture and encourage continuous improvement in workplace practices.
•	Assist project teams with safety planning, mobilisation requirements, and compliance documentation.
•	Maintain safety records, registers, inspection reports, and incident databases.
•	Liaise with clients, contractors, and regulatory bodies regarding health and safety matters where required.
•	Ensure compliance with workplace health, safety, environmental, and quality management systems.

Skills and Experience
•	Minimum 1-2 years of full-time experience as a Safety Advisor, Occupational Health and Safety Advisor, or similar WHS role.
•	Relevant qualification in Occupational Health and Safety, Workplace Health and Safety, or a related discipline.
•	Strong knowledge of Australian WHS legislation, safety management systems, and risk management principles.
•	Experience working within mining, construction, engineering, maintenance, or industrial environments is highly regarded.
•	Ability to conduct workplace inspections, audits, investigations, and safety training.
•	Strong communication, consultation, and problem-solving skills.
•	Excellent attention to detail and ability to manage multiple priorities.
•	Ability to work independently and collaboratively with project teams.
•	Proficiency in Microsoft Office and safety management systems.

What We Offer
•	Full-time, permanent employment.
•	Competitive salary of $100,000 – $130,000 per annum.
•	Opportunities to work on major mining, shutdown, engineering, and industrial projects.
•	Ongoing professional development and career progression.
•	Supportive team environment with long-term career opportunities.
